facts.text: Olympic Village was built to house 2,800 athletes, coaches, and officials for the 2010 Winter Olympics and Paralympics.
The Village spans over a million square feet and contains more than a thousand residential units, making it one of Vancouver’s largest mixed‑use communities.
Completed on 1 November 2009, the Village was handed over to the Vancouver Organizing Committee just weeks before the Games opened.
After the Games, the accommodations were converted into permanent residential housing, creating a vibrant neighborhood that now sits at the core of Southeast False Creek.
The Village’s design earned it North America’s first LEED Platinum certification, a first for a large urban development.
A former industrial site, the Village sparked the revitalization of False Creek, turning a neglected waterfront into a lively community hub.
